EVM per-transaction gas price cap and native reserve, and Solana priority-fee cap and lamport reserve, are required configuration fields. The literal atomic value '1' is a configuration error for any minimum or gas cap. The signed message is validated again before broadcast. There are exactly two signer identities, Operations EVM and Operations Solana; signing occurs outside the Node process unless a recorded owner exception applies. Edge case: an unknown target, mismatched address bytes, changed message, invalid co-signer, stale blockhash, missing gas cap, placeholder configuration, timeout, a provider-specific binding digest mismatch, an attempt to construct a provider-specific policy field from candidate-derived semantics, an attempt to use synthetic binding authority for live execution, or secret-bearing signer path refuses signing. Live Collector authority additionally requires exactly two immutable independently owner-approved purchase and buyback anchors authenticated by the frozen release manifest. Registry bytes, their adjacent digest, a configurable path, or environment selection cannot establish authority. All existing synthetic isolation and transaction validation rules remain enforced. Actual binding values and live transactions require separate explicit approval. The independently pinned Collector generatePack purchase profile additionally permits exactly compute-unit limit, provider-signed Memo, checked SPL transfer, and compute-unit price in that order. Its Memo appends the fixed :open suffix to the durable request memo; its checked transfer repeats the identical operator authority with identical signer and writable flags. For this profile, only the original candidate blockhash may be extracted to request independent RPC validity evidence. No candidate-derived validity claim is trusted, no block height is invented, and the original message bytes remain unchanged. RPC validity must be true for that exact blockhash at or above an immutable minimum observed slot. Recovery and pre-broadcast validation refresh that independent observation; the approval digest binds the immutable rule sidecar, including its minimum slot, so reconstruction cannot weaken it. Existing legacy purchase and buyback profiles remain unchanged. The separately identified Collector Core buyback profile additionally permits exactly compute-unit limit, MPL Core TransferV1, compute-unit price, associated-token-account createIdempotent, checked SPL proceeds transfer, and a fixed :buyback memo in that order. The provider is the fee payer and first signer; Operations remains the independently finalized asset owner and second signer, never a provider-controlled identity. The policy binds the exact opened Core asset, independently approved collection and recipient, fixed Core and token programs, exact no-payload TransferV1 bytes and account flags, canonical Operations proceeds ATA, provider proceeds source, settlement mint and decimals, persisted quote and minimum, durable buyback memo, compute limits and provider priority-fee cap before candidate acquisition. The exact checked proceeds transfer must equal the persisted quote and meet the minimum in the same atomic transaction as the asset transfer. No operator native payment, approval, delegate, extra instruction, alternate asset or destination is permitted. Original blockhash validity is independently observed and bound to an immutable minimum slot, refreshed before signing and broadcast, with byte-identical recovery. Existing legacy buyback profiles remain unchanged. Public historical transactions prove structure only; actual release values require independent source/runtime correspondence, separate owner-approved live anchors and frozen release authority. No signature, broadcast, purchase or sale is authorized by this profile approval.
requirements.measurement: Negative fixtures for EVM and both Solana formats prove each allowlist field is enforced; configuration tests require each explicit minimum and gas cap and reject a literal atomic value '1'; parity fixtures prove the adapters decoder produces hookemon.transaction-policy.v1 version 1; signer tests prove external invocation, timeout visibility, two-identity separation, and pre-broadcast revalidation; provider-specific purchase and buyback policy fixtures prove refusal on a binding digest mismatch, on an unknown or malformed binding field, and on any factory input that carries candidate transaction bytes or decoded candidate semantics. Focused fixtures prove immutable binding authority across provider awaits, purchase binding to admitted per-pack facts, buyback binding to finalized open facts and a separately authorized sell decision, and refusal before intent or provider mutation when binding authority is absent or mismatched. An isolated ordinary-CLI full-flow fixture uses independently fixed synthetic bindings and isolated external services; negative fixtures prove that synthetic authority cannot enable live endpoints or live signer capabilities. This proof does not constitute approval of real provider binding values. Live registry tests accept only exact release-anchored stage bindings and reject missing approval evidence, modified paths or digests, substituted manifests, and synthetic/live mixing before mutation. Exact generatePack profile fixtures reject changed instruction order, Memo suffix, duplicate authority, signer flags, amounts, destinations, or missing/corrupt provider signatures. Independent RPC fixtures reject invalid or mismatched original hashes and regressing observation slots; recovery fixtures reject reconstruction with a lowered immutable minimum slot while preserving the original transaction message. Core buyback tests use an authentic public transaction as a structural reference, reject changed fee payer, owner, asset, collection, recipient, proceeds source/destination, amount, memo, flags, program, order, extra instruction, failed provider signature, expired original blockhash and weakened recovery rule; prove no provider call without trusted bindings and no repeated signature on recovery.

requirements.title: Cycle-attributed operations-wallet stages
requirements.statement: Given a planned cycle, when the runner executes it, then its ordered stages are eligibility-snapshot, claim-process, outbound, purchase, open, epic-gate, buyback, return, and payout. The runner persists the immutable cycle mode before stage execution and production services refuse rehearsal cycles while rehearsal services refuse production cycles. Before signing a purchase, it persists typed {chainId, assetId, decimals, amountAtomic} values for unitPriceAtomic, totalAtomic, and boundedOverheadAtomic plus positive integer-string quantity; totalAtomic equals quantity multiplied by unitPriceAtomic, all money fields share the same asset identity, and policy reserves totalAtomic plus boundedOverheadAtomic. A card carved into a held position no longer keeps the cycle terminally held. Return and the main payout bridge and distribute only settled, cycle-attributed proceeds, list excluded positions in their evidence, and allow COMPLETED with open positions or a zero-proceeds, zero-manifest COMPLETED result when every card is held. A completed record with open positions remains one active DurableCycleStore entry for supplementary recovery even though scheduler admission skips it. The 16-entry store supports the default `maxHeldPositions` 10 when positions span completed cycles; a configuration above that verified-safe value of 10 is refused at admission until post-completion position archival or a measured store-capacity exemption exists. Outbound can use only the cycle's claimed principal. No bucket can fund another cycle. The custody ledger records finalized observed current balances separately from obligations, counts unresolved principal exactly once, records expected cycle assets separately from unattributed external deposits, and pauses new claims for those deposits. For the canonical EVM native ETH row only, hookemon.custody-ledger.v3 with an independently finalized native balance observation carries a verifiedCurrentBalance (CustodyBalanceObservationV1 | null) and a singular expectedCycleAsset (TypedAmount | null, never a collection), and unvaluedExposure becomes true whenever verifiedCurrentBalance is null while unresolved principal is positive or any current-custody bucket is nonzero. A pure, two-independent-source finalized-observation combiner (packages/adapters/src/solana-custody-balance-observation.mjs#combineFinalizedBalanceObservation and #observeFinalizedBalanceWithRetry) is an allowed evidence-construction contract for a future non-EVM verifiedCurrentBalance; it is not itself a durable producer, a canonical chain/asset identity source, a custody-ledger writer, a valuation, or live readiness proof, and constructing its output does not by itself satisfy this requirement. Any non-native-EVM row stays on hookemon.custody-ledger.v1, or, if migrated to v2, stays permanently unvalued and fail-closed under the same admission rule until a separately approved evidence producer exists for it. Native principal and gas share the ETH asset identity but occupy separate reservation and cost buckets; spendable principal excludes the gas reserve and unpaid obligations. Only finalized cycle-attributed native payment proofs may become an Operations ETH credit or payout basis. A direct native payment is proved from the persisted signed transaction identity, exact sender, recipient, value and calldata, successful receipt and canonical finalized block; a trusted hook post-payment event proves a claim. Internal Relay return or refund proof additionally authenticates emitter runtime, request linkage, decoded recipient/value and failure propagation. Missing proof leaves proceeds unavailable. No wallet-wide delta or fabricated ERC20 Transfer event proves a native credit. Historical USDG journals remain readable but cannot resume through the native runtime or be rescaled; native cycles use fresh identities. Edge case: an unattributed inbound deposit, cross-mode request, mismatched purchase total, bridge-funded cross-cycle action, a non-native-EVM v2 row treated as valued without an approved producer, or attempt to finance one cycle with another fails closed. New native cycles atomically persist a versioned rewardSelection snapshot in cycle-opened, binding cycleId, configurationRevision, rewardRecipientLimit and a canonical domain-separated digest. Resume reads only that snapshot; later configuration edits cannot change it. Existing native cycle-opened records without this field remain on the historical all-holder path without mutation or digest changes. Supplementary payouts retain the original cycle selection.
requirements.measurement: End-to-end fakes and fork tests assert exact nine-stage order, typed-amount validation, purchase arithmetic and reserve, immutable mode isolation, held-position carve-out, settled-proceeds-only return and payout, all-held zero completion, completed-record supplementary recovery without reopening the main cycle, interleaved-cycle isolation, asset separation, cycle-attribution keys, claimed-principal-only outbound, proceeds-delta-only return, finality before completion, observed-balance and obligation conservation, one-time unresolved-principal accounting, pause on unattributed deposits, and independent gas reserves; custody-ledger fixtures additionally prove the EVM native ETH row's unvaluedExposure admission rule on a null verifiedCurrentBalance with nonzero unresolved claim or current-custody bucket, the singular non-collection expectedCycleAsset write-time refusal of a second unresolved return leg, and that a non-native-EVM row constructed as v2 remains permanently unvalued absent an approved producer. Native tests reject wrong request/emitter/runtime/value, failed internal calls, unrelated deposits, stale or reorged receipts, duplicate proofs, old USDG resume and any principal spending that consumes the gas reserve. Test atomic opening, policy digest tampering, changed operator settings before and after restart, historic absent-field replay, cross-cycle policy substitution and supplementary reuse of the original selection.

requirements.title: Fail-closed epic-card hold policy
requirements.statement: Given a returned card and a buyback offer validated by REQ-collector-crypt-adapter-1, when the card is in the existing documented epic tier (`prizeTier === '1'`) and is eligible for sale, then it becomes a held position exactly when offerAtomic multiplied by 100 is less than insuredValueAtomic multiplied by 40; equality sells. Other documented tiers do not enter this 40-percent threshold branch. Missing or invalid data, missing mint, rarity conflict, buyback unavailable, changed quote, wrong mint, or an unverified insured-value reconciliation creates a HELD_* position, never auto-sells, raises an alarm, and records the card's attributed purchase-cost share, typed insured value or null, reason, evidence digest, and opening time. A held position is removed from the cycle's settled path, not from its attribution. Its owner decision is idempotent and bound to position ID, evidence digest, request ID, and position revision: `keep-holding` has no settlement effect, and `sell` starts its supplementary settlement. A held card does not independently block a new claim.
requirements.measurement: BigInt and lifecycle tests cover the prizeTier-1 strict inequality and equality, non-epic tier behavior, every fail-closed HELD_* class, immutable position evidence, insured-value reconciliation failure, per-position owner-decision idempotency, cycle completion with settled cards, and a held card that remains counted without independently refusing a new claim.

requirements.title: Pre-claim finalized eligibility snapshot
requirements.statement: Given a planned cycle, when eligibility-snapshot runs as the first cycle stage, then before claimProcess the runner pins a finalized block and hash, replays HKMN Transfer logs from deployment through that block, reconciles mint minus burn against the launch manifest, rechecks the block hash after scanning, and proves log completeness through an independent second source or archive RPC. It excludes zero and burn addresses, Hook, PoolManager, custody, Operations, Treasury, Programmable, launch contracts, and historical role holders while allowing contract holders to receive native ETH at their own addresses, with bounded native payout simulation before claim. It evaluates recipient count, measured gas, gas-price cap, native balance, and transaction count before claim. Edge case: a reorg, incomplete or unordered logs, supply mismatch, missing source, or infeasible payout envelope prevents the claim. For cycles with an explicit rewardSelection snapshot, selection follows complete verified holder replay and exclusions: rank positive direct HKMN balances descending, break ties by normalized address ascending, and retain at most rewardRecipientLimit holders. Persist selected entries in canonical address order, configured limit and actual selectedCount separately, and enough full-holder evidence to reconstruct ranking and supply reconciliation. The allocation denominator is the sum of selected balances; excluded and unselected balances are excluded from that denominator but remain in full-supply evidence. Evaluate native recipient, transaction and gas feasibility against the selected set; never silently reduce the chosen set to make an infeasible envelope pass. Cycles without the snapshot keep the historical all-holder semantics.
requirements.measurement: Snapshot tests inject each log and reorg fault, compare deterministic manifests, prove supply reconciliation and hash recheck, and assert no claim request is prepared before the feasibility envelope passes. Cover excess, fewer, absent, excluded, tied and zero-weight holders; reproduce selection and selection evidence digests independently; reject count, policy, holder evidence and supply mismatch. Preserve full replay evidence and prove selected plus unselected plus excluded balances equals supply.

requirements.title: Finalized direct holder payout
requirements.statement: Given a finalized cycle-attributed Operations native ETH credit and its frozen eligibility manifest, when the main payout begins, then the runner sends direct native ETH value payments only for settled cards through the durable chain-attempt contract: PREPARED(requestDigest, policyDigest, fencingToken), SIGNED(rawSignedBytesHash, nonceOrBlockhash, txHash, approvedSemanticsDigest), BROADCAST, FINALIZED, or REFUSED(reason, fencingToken). The first accepted sell decision for one held position atomically creates exactly one supplementary settlement keyed by that position's ID, starting a supplementary buyback, return leg for only that position's attributed proceeds, and supplementary payout with manifest ID `<cycleId>:supplementary:<n>`; an exact replay of that same sell request returns the identical settlement and manifest identifier, a conflicting or later sell request for an already-settled or in-flight position fails, and a resolved position can never create a second manifest. The settlement persists the digest of the original completed eligibility snapshot; its RETURN_BROADCAST boundary persists the exact finalized return and return binding as a payout-source digest, and binds that return and any permitted dust source to a one-time atomic consumption record shared across every supplementary manifest for that position, so at most one supplementary manifest is ever funded per held position and per return source. The supplementary payout accepts only that snapshot and source, becomes immutable at its first broadcast, and pays every recipient exactly once for that manifest. It uses zero/null dust unless that same atomic position-aware supplementary dust-consumption transition has bound an unconsumed original-cycle source. The wallet-wide nonce lock covers claim, outbound, return, main payout, and supplementary payout. SIGNED records retain immutable retrievable signed bytes and recover after restart. A dropped BROADCAST resolves by receipt search or a replacement using the same nonce and calldata, after revalidating the persisted approvedSemanticsDigest. It marks paid only after proof of the exact successful finalized transaction matched to persisted signed bytes/hash, source, recipient, value and calldata; a recipient may forward ETH and its ending balance is not payment proof. Rejected recipient calls become quarantine liabilities without blocking the rest of a manifest; dust carry is durable and atomically consumed and written between cycles. Edge case: a crash between supplementary broadcast and finality, duplicate recipient, nonce collision, replacement with different calldata, changed approval digest, dropped broadcast, rejecting recipient, or dust replay cannot create a double payment or silently change either manifest. Selected native cycles use versioned manifests and payout plans that bind the frozen selection evidence. For each selected holder, allocate floor(distributablePool * directHkmnBalance / selectedBalanceTotal), preserving current native dust carry, gas reservation, authorization and quarantine rules. Do not port historical largest-remainder redistribution. Unselected holders receive no payment and accrue no payout liability for this cycle. A selected holder with a zero rounded allocation remains selected but produces no value transfer. Historical native plans and signed or finalized payments retain byte-identical contents and digest verification.
requirements.measurement: Node tests cover restart at every main and supplementary payout boundary, durable signed-record recovery, approval-digest revalidation, exact finalized native transaction identity, value and successful execution, immutable manifests, the original snapshot and return source reused by a supplementary manifest, exactly-once supplementary transfers after restart, exactly one settlement and manifest per positionId across restart, an exact replay of the same sell request ID with identical evidence returning the identical settlement and manifest identifier, a sell request with a different request ID after the first accepted sell failing without creating or funding a second manifest, a second manifest attempted for the same position/return source failing, same-nonce-and-calldata replacement, receipt search for a dropped broadcast, wallet-wide nonce fencing, refusal fencing, rejecting-recipient quarantine with continuation, failed gas counted as cost rather than principal, and no automatic retry, redirect or WETH fallback for terminal REFUSED recipients, durable dust carry, and recipient counts through the verified feasibility envelope. Execute the actual native payout handler on an isolated local EVM for N=100,200,300,400,500,600 with more than N eligible holders and sufficient principal for positive allocations. Assert exactly one finalized payment per selected holder, no unselected payment, principal plus dust conservation, gas accounting, unique nonces and interruption recovery without duplicates. Separate zero-rounding tests assert selectedCount differs from payableRecipientCount without fabricated payments. No live wallet or mainnet broadcast is allowed for this acceptance evidence.

requirements.title: Atomic policy controls and rehearsal mode
requirements.statement: Given an Operations-wallet cycle, when it reaches a claim, purchase, or signature boundary, then the policy engine atomically maps dashboard caps and allowlists to micro-USD controls, enforces a rolling 24-hour spend ledger, maximum cycles per day, per-cycle cap, rolling realized-plus-at-risk loss cap, maximum outstanding custody, and an execution pause or kill switch before every signature. It also admits a claim while open held positions remain unless their count is greater than or equal to `maxHeldPositions` or their value exceeds `maxHeldValueMicroUsd`; that refusal is `HELD_LIMIT`. Held value is attributed purchase cost in USD micro-units. Insured amounts remain informational and cannot replace that control value; neither a Solana stablecoin amount nor ETH wei is assumed to be USD. `maxHeldPositions` defaults to 10 with range 0 through 10, the verified capacity-safe maximum for the 16-entry DurableCycleStore; a configuration above 10 is refused until post-completion position archival or a measured store-capacity exemption exists. `maxHeldValueMicroUsd` defaults to `5000000000`. Pending epic decisions do not independently refuse a claim. Unattributed and unvalued custody remain fail-closed. It verifies all persisted purchase fields: unitPriceAtomic, quantity, totalAtomic, and boundedOverheadAtomic; enforces totalAtomic equals quantity multiplied by unitPriceAtomic; and reserves totalAtomic plus boundedOverheadAtomic. It evaluates finalized observed balances and obligations separately, with unresolved principal counted once. The existing USD outer rails remain 55 per unit, 165 per cycle and 495 per rolling day, with tighter owner limits preserved. Existing unit and aggregate Relay quote admission binds each USD valuation to the exact fetched request, quote digest, chain, asset, atomic amount and validity window, using integer decimal arithmetic with costs/exposure rounded up and proceeds rounded down. Committed spend remains at validated USD cost basis; unresolved liquid ETH or USDC exposure requires fresh bound valuation before additional risk and cannot double-count existing reservations. The policy separately checks exact ETH transaction maxima and the gas reserve. Missing valuation refuses new risk but not reconciliation or separately authorized recovery. The owner plans an initial EUR 250 contribution for one or two controlled native mainnet test cycles. Complete-process affordability need not be proven before functional testing; actual contributions, costs and remaining balances are reconciled before any separately authorized additional funding. External owner capital is counted once, not recycled turnover or every production cycle. Per-action USD caps, native transaction maxima, gas reserves and manual cycle approval remain mandatory. No second budget helper or onchain oracle is introduced. The first N production cycles require digest-bound manual approval. Cycle mode is persisted at creation and immutable; production and rehearsal services refuse the other mode. The production return minimum is the explicit TypedAmount {chainId: "4663", assetId: "native", decimals: 18, amountAtomic: "0"}; it means no general return minimum. No minimum or gas cap has an implicit atomic-unit default. Edge case: pause, cap breach, missing manual approval, held-position count or value limit, foreign mode, mismatched purchase arithmetic, placeholder minimum or gas cap, or unattributed or unvalued custody refuses the next irreversible action.
requirements.measurement: Policy and runner tests prove atomic cap application, rolling-window accounting, loss and custody limits, held-position count and value `HELD_LIMIT` refusal, a `maxHeldPositions` configuration at the 10/11/15/16 boundaries proving 10 accepted and every value above 10 refused, pending-decision non-refusal, purchase-field validation and reserve, observed-balance and obligation separation, pause-before-signature, digest binding, immutable mode isolation, explicit zero production return minimum, required gas-cap configuration, restart evidence, and no duplicate effect.

requirements.title: Collector Crypt documented response contract
requirements.statement: Given a Collector Crypt pack or buyback response, when the adapter validates it, then prize tiers are numeric 1 through 4, buyback amounts are configured Solana stablecoin base units with six decimals, contains accepts an integer or numeric string, and openPack uses the documented idempotent operation. insured_value is usable only when reconciliation proves its unit against the machine instantBuyback percentage; otherwise the card becomes a HELD_DATA_UNVERIFIED held position. Edge case: an unsupported tier, malformed contains value, non-idempotent open result, missing unit proof, or reconciliation mismatch cannot authorize purchase, sale, or payout.
requirements.measurement: Adapter and lifecycle fixtures cover all four tiers, integer and numeric-string contains values, documented idempotent openPack replay, configured Solana stablecoin base-unit accounting, insured-value reconciliation, and a HELD_DATA_UNVERIFIED held position on every missing or contradictory proof.

requirements.title: Provider-bound fee and launch readiness
requirements.statement: The assisted native launch revision uses the inclusive 300 basis-point split of 20 Programmable, 30 treasury and 250 process. The immutable Programmable recipient on chain 4663 is 0xD88539d3c4C460136a733A3Fd60cf6BF269079da. Historical FEE-01 decisions and submissions remain historical evidence. Provider integration must verify this exact custom cumulative-remainder model; an additive standard fee profile or per-trade ceiling cannot replace it. Code readiness does not authorize deployment, signing, broadcast, funding or launch. Launch timing and optional initial purchase remain unset and are not preparation requirements.
requirements.measurement: Recorded provider acceptance, probes, and release-gate tests prove each required evidence field, the separate readiness flags, the accepted fee share, and refusal of every unresolved or contradictory response.

requirements.title: Phase 3 code and live readiness separation
requirements.statement: Given a Phase 3 candidate, when release evidence is evaluated, then cleanroom, deployment-manifest, control-dependency, traceability, non-skipping fork proof, current-head canary, and runner evidence establish code readiness only. launchEligible additionally requires current provider admission, exact graph and binding evidence, operational canaries, and all owner-gated live prerequisites. Edge case: a green local build, dry run, or CI result without live readiness remains non-authorizing.
requirements.measurement: Release tests exercise every boolean readiness combination, assert a named blocker for each false prerequisite, and prove no code-ready state is reported as launch eligible.

requirements.title: Pre-signature canaries and durable alerts
requirements.statement: Given any irreversible signature request, when the policy engine evaluates it, then it checks chain id, contract and proxy runtime hashes, native ETH identity and 18-decimal unit binding, funded native principal and distinct gas reserve, and bounded recipient-call feasibility, roles, protocol fee, router and quoter hashes, provider-policy digest, nonce or blockhash, gas reserves, pause and loss limits, and unattributed custody. A detected drift blocks signing, creates one durable deduplicated alert, and remains observable without exposing credentials. Edge case: any missing, stale, contradictory, or unverified canary result fails closed before a signature exists.
requirements.measurement: Canary tests inject each drift class and assert signature refusal, one persisted alert per condition, redaction, recovery only after the current evidence passes, and no duplicate alert across restart.

requirements.title: Bounded transient recovery classification
requirements.statement: Given a provider or chain attempt that fails before, during, or after an external effect, when the repository classifies its recovery path, then it assigns exactly one of three classes: semantic-invalid (the request itself is wrong and requires a terminal HELD_* state with an owner decision), effect-ambiguous (the external outcome cannot yet be distinguished and the attempt stays observation-only until canonical evidence resolves it), or proven-pre-effect-transient (no external effect occurred and the identical approved intent may retry automatically once the blocking condition clears). A Relay quote that expires before any request or signature is proven-pre-effect-transient: it stays nonterminal with no cycle terminal state and no attempt, persists the expired quote identity and deadline, and only after re-proving no signed or broadcast attempt exists does policy/admission atomically select one replacement quote for the same claimed principal under `refresh-after-readmission`; it never silently substitutes a quote once signed bytes exist. A Solana chain attempt whose blockhash expires past its validity boundary is effect-ambiguous: it stays `BROADCAST` and observation-only until reconciliation either finalizes it or produces canonical expired-and-unlanded proof, and only then creates exactly one linked replacement attempt with a fresh blockhash under `reconcile-then-replace`, retaining the original signed bytes and signature permanently. A wallet lease or fencing token lost strictly before the provider or signature capability boundary is proven-pre-effect-transient: it stays `NOT_SENT` with no cycle terminal state, and a newly fenced owner may retry the identical prepared request digest exactly once under `retry-same-request-under-new-lease`. Lease loss discovered after a provider-mutation capability boundary was already reached is a distinct, effect-ambiguous class: it is reclassified `SENT_UNKNOWN`, stays observation-only under `reconcile-before-retry`, and forbids any automatic retry or new provider mutation until canonical reconciliation resolves the prior attempt; it never shares the pre-boundary class's tuple. Lease loss discovered after a signing capability boundary was already reached is instead governed by the durable chain-attempt contract's own `PREPARED`/`SIGNED`/`BROADCAST`/`REFUSED` states from REQ-cycle-repository-1, not by `SENT_UNKNOWN`, because a chain attempt already carries its own state machine for that ambiguity. An external signer denial that provably occurred before any signature could have been produced is proven-pre-effect-transient: it stays `NOT_SENT` with no cycle terminal state, persists a bounded redacted signer-unavailable reason and next retry time, and retries the identical request against the same approved signer identity after bounded backoff under `retry-after-signer-readiness`. A sign-only external signer timeout may retry the identical signing attempt only for the verified owned Keychain broker, whose separate, distinctly guarded broadcast capability the checked-in source proves its sign operation never reaches. That retry is proven-pre-effect-transient only when the exact unsigned wire bytes, signer role/account identity, request digest, policy/authorization digest, and validity context were durably persisted before that broker's sign-only operation was first invoked; the retry reuses those exact durably bound values, never regenerates the provider transaction, blockhash, nonce, memo, or policy under the retry's identity, and never asserts the prior attempt produced no signature — a signature returned by either attempt is captured exactly once through the existing signed-bytes recovery record, which rejects materially different signing material, under `retry-sign-only-with-durable-binding`. This identical-byte, idempotent-retry guarantee is enabled only once focused evidence proves it for that exact broker contract; it grants no broadcast authority, and a subsequent broadcast or provider-send outcome that cannot be distinguished remains its own observation-only `SENT_UNKNOWN` or chain-attempt state, never retried as an unsigned request. Every opaque or external-module signer timeout keeps the existing no-automatic-retry, terminal whole-cycle class, because canonical chain observation cannot recover or rule out an unbroadcast signature for it; automatic sign-only retry is not extended to any other signer by this revision, and a future signer can receive it only through a later owner-approved spec revision bound to that exact signer contract, never by an implementation-time claim of equivalence. Edge case: a stale fenced owner performs no effect after fence failure; a class assignment never exports a key, substitutes a signer, or creates a new request; and semantic-invalid classes (wrong-asset, wrong-recipient, cross-cycle attribution failure, conflicting canonical evidence) keep their existing terminal HELD_* owner-decision contract unchanged.
